cells.tense: You read the room's proportions and adjust them while the evening is still going.
cells.act: let the old form go so the next one can come
cells.ask: Pick one practice your people keep that has finished its work, and end it plainly, whenever the next gathering comes. Say what it was for when it began, and leave the space it frees empty — no replacement yet.
cells.core:
Among the customs your group keeps, you can feel when something has stopped being owed and adjust it plainly, without keeping a ledger in your head. The handovers stay clean and the old forms stay light enough to carry. People lean on that evenness and rarely notice someone is adjusting it.

What flows out of it is endings that are just endings. A custom or a way of doing things can finish, and you can close it without decorating the end, trusting the next form to come in its own time. You'll still reach for it before it arrives. When one of your people's customs is done, end it where they can see, and leave the space it frees as space.

cells.verb: weighing what each person is owed and settling it plainly
cells.place: among the shared customs and handed-down ways a group keeps

cells.tense: You will be tallying what each person owes before the next gathering even begins.
cells.act: keep it at its real size when you are asked to shrink it
cells.ask: When someone wants a custom made smaller or finished on their clock, give it its true size in one sentence — what it actually was — then stop there and go on with your day.
cells.core:
What runs evenly in the group's shared ways is turning into an account. You track who showed up, who repaid, who owes the gathering what, and the scale keeps moving, because a scale that moves can't rest. You're braced for a settling a tally can't reach.

Endurance is what to pick up instead of the count. You can bear weight without tightening around it, and hold a custom at its true size when someone wants it smaller or wants it finished sooner. You'll want to argue the balance once more. Say only what it actually was, and then go on with your evening.

cells.tense: You once learned that asking for what you were owed made the room unsafe, and you have not gone back for it.
cells.act: do the small practice again, alone, today
cells.ask: Take a song, a recipe, or a phrase from your people's ways and do it alone today, at whatever hour suits. Repeat it past what's needed, and ask it for nothing back.
cells.core:
Where the shared ways run, you've stopped claiming your part. You keep the customs and show up for the people, and when something is yours by right, you let it pass, because asking has not been safe. You're still holding up the room's ways, keeping what's given without taking what belongs to you.

What's starved here is a steady practice of your own. Pick a song, a recipe, or a phrase from your people's ways, short enough that it asks nothing back, and do it alone today. Repeat it once past what's needed. Not for a feeling or a result — the light stays lit by attention, and attention is what a person stands in when they finally ask for what they're owed.

cells.tense: You are adding up what each person owes while the pen is down, and you'd say you are not counting.
cells.act: notice what you already know before you reason about it
cells.ask: When a gathering leaves that sour pull in the gut, notice it before building a case. Name the first plain fact to yourself, then set the whole thing down and go do something with your hands.
cells.core:
You keep the shared ways running and you'd tell anyone you carry no account of who gave what. The tally runs anyway, and it shows up as a flat feeling toward the very people and customs you keep, with no story you'd recognize as counting. It colors the room you're most at home in.

The first plain fact is available before the argument is. Stop in the next gathering that leaves that cold pull, and give the earliest thing you noticed its due instead of walling it in reasons. Then set it down — one clean move is enough for now, and the case was the point only if you make it one.
